Subject: Optimize toolkit pricing: quantization & credits approach

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Based on the usage profile you shared (burst-y daytime inference, 300M tokens/mo peak, majority of short chat responses, ~20% long-form generation), we sketched two pragmatic approaches to reduce unit cost while keeping latency within your SLOs:

1) Credits-first (hosted) model + batching/caching guidance
- Keep the hosting on Redwood API. Provide a credit bundle that roofs your burst needs and gives a lower per-token rate when credits are consumed.
- Apply automatic prefix caching for common prompts and conversation warmup to reduce repeated KV work.

2) Quantization-forward (dedicated/dedicated-lite) model
- Recommend int8/4-bit quantized weights for customer-dedicated pools. Best when long-form tokens dominate.
- We estimate a 35-45% per-token cost reduction for heavy-generation paths, with a small latency delta depending on instance class.

Attached: a working econ model (Optimize_Econ_Model_v2.xlsx) with a simple simulator (batch sizes, cache hit rates, quantization multipliers).

Quick asks: can you confirm a target monthly committed spend range (rough number) and whether you need enterprise SLAs for a public-cloud vs private VPC deployment? That will change whether we recommend credits + hosted or a dedicated quantized pool.

Sara —

Appreciate the concrete asks. I updated the econ model and attached a one-pager (Redwood_SOW_template.pdf) you can pass to procurement. High level:

Summary (attached and pasted below):
- Conservative (50k req / mo): Hosted credits bundle (6mo prepay) -> estimated $1,800/mo effective cost; minimal setup.
- Expected (200k req / mo): Hosted + Optimize Toolkit advisory bundle -> estimated $6,700/mo; includes automated prefix caching and batching guidance, monthly cadenced prompts/eval checks.
- Aggressive (600k req / mo): Dedicated quantized pool (reserved) -> estimated $16k/mo committed (12mo), with ~40% token cost reduction vs non-quantized hosted.

Concessions: for first-year committed deals we typically consider a stepped discount structure: 8% on first-year committed spend for packages >= $100k ARR, or an accelerated credits rebate for a 12-month prepay. If you prefer credits vs percent discount, we can propose an additional credit tranche equal to 3% of the commitment.

Quality delta: our internal evals on Redwood-Open-XL show negligible instruction-following regression at int8 for short-to-medium outputs; int4 shows small degradation on subjective metrics (fluency for long-form >2k tokens) for some prompt families. I attached a short simulation (batching_cache_simulation.csv) and the assumptions in the spreadsheet. We can share example eval slices if helpful.

Next steps I propose:
- I will send a concise proposal summary (one-pager + econ tab) for procurement by EOD tomorrow.
- Rishi (cc'd) will scope operational support and SLA options if you want a dedicated pool.
- If procurement wants a legal redline, we can return an SOW within 48 hours.

Rishi / Dev —

Looping you in here with the latest from FinLytics. They asked for the three-scenario cost table and a first-year concession. I sketched two options in the attached econ model and one-pager already sent. Procurement said they expect a blended cap for 12 months.

My recommended negotiation posture to close this quarter:
- Offer credits-first for the first 6 months (hosted) with a 4% credit tranche on sign (effectively a small up-front rebate) so procurement has predictable spend.
- If they hit the aggressive scenario by month 3, convert to a reserved quantized pool with an early-termination pro-rata credit and a 7% commit discount for the remaining term.

This lets us: 1) avoid heavy upfront infra commitments, 2) prove caching/batching improvements, and 3) lock in a larger dedication if they scale quickly.

If you’re OK with those concession bands I’ll send a formal proposal to procurement (procurement@finlytics.com) with the SOW and redline path.

Thanks,
Kimberly
